claim: In malaria, rosetting is described as a phenomenon where an infected erythrocyte (IRBC) is attached to uninfected erythrocytes (URBC).
source: In malaria, rosetting is described as a phenomenon where an infected erythrocyte (IRBC) is attached to uninfected erythrocytes (URBC).
evidence: This is a definitional statement provided in the abstract without specific experimental data or citations in this sentence.

claim: In some studies, rosetting has been associated with malaria pathogenesis.
source: In some studies, rosetting has been associated with malaria pathogenesis.
evidence: This statement references prior research findings without providing specific citations in this sentence, drawing on established literature.

claim: IGFBP7 is a protein secreted by monocytes in response to parasite stimulation.
source: Using a step-by-step approach, we identified IGFBP7, a protein secreted by monocytes in response to parasite stimulation, as a rosette-stimulator for Plasmodium falciparum- and P. vivax-IRBC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including mass spectrometry analysis and ELISA quantification of IGFBP7 secretion by monocytes.

claim: IGFBP7 acts as a rosette-stimulator for Plasmodium falciparum-IRBC.
source: Using a step-by-step approach, we identified IGFBP7, a protein secreted by monocytes in response to parasite stimulation, as a rosette-stimulator for Plasmodium falciparum- and P. vivax-IRBC.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that addition of recombinant IGFBP7 increased rosetting rates in P. falciparum cultures.

claim: IGFBP7 acts as a rosette-stimulator for P. vivax-IRBC.
source: Using a step-by-step approach, we identified IGFBP7, a protein secreted by monocytes in response to parasite stimulation, as a rosette-stimulator for Plasmodium falciparum- and P. vivax-IRBC.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that addition of recombinant IGFBP7 increased rosetting rates in P. vivax cultures.

claim: IGFBP7-mediated rosette-stimulation was rapid.
source: IGFBP7-mediated rosette-stimulation was rapid yet reversible.
evidence: This is supported by time course experiments showing significant rosette stimulation as fast as 15 minutes after IGFBP7 exposure.

claim: IGFBP7-mediated rosette-stimulation was reversible.
source: IGFBP7-mediated rosette-stimulation was rapid yet reversible.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that removal of IGFBP7 from the system reverted rosetting rates to baseline values within 15 minutes.

claim: Type I rosetting involves direct interaction of rosetting ligands on IRBC and receptors on URBC.
source: Unlike type I rosetting that involves direct interaction of rosetting ligands on IRBC and receptors on URBC, the IGFBP7-mediated, type II rosetting requires two additional serum factors, namely von Willebrand factor and thrombospondin-1.
evidence: This is a characterization based on established knowledge of classical rosetting mechanisms.

claim: IGFBP7-mediated type II rosetting requires von Willebrand factor.
source: Unlike type I rosetting that involves direct interaction of rosetting ligands on IRBC and receptors on URBC, the IGFBP7-mediated, type II rosetting requires two additional serum factors, namely von Willebrand factor and thrombospondin-1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that anti-VWF antibodies blocked IGFBP7-mediated rosetting and that VWF was required in serum-free conditions for IGFBP7 to stimulate rosetting.

claim: IGFBP7-mediated type II rosetting requires thrombospondin-1.
source: Unlike type I rosetting that involves direct interaction of rosetting ligands on IRBC and receptors on URBC, the IGFBP7-mediated, type II rosetting requires two additional serum factors, namely von Willebrand factor and thrombospondin-1.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that anti-TSP-1 antibodies blocked IGFBP7-mediated rosetting and that TSP-1 was required in serum-free conditions for IGFBP7 to stimulate rosetting.

claim: IGFBP7-induced type II rosetting hampers phagocytosis of IRBC by host phagocytes.
source: Importantly, the IGFBP7-induced type II rosetting hampers phagocytosis of IRBC by host phagocytes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing that IRBC phagocytosis rates by monocytes and THP-1 cells were significantly reduced when IRBC were pre-incubated with IGFBP7.

claim: P. falciparum modifies the infected erythrocyte rheology by increasing rigidity.
source: Along its intraerythrocytic development, Plasmodium spp. modifies the infected erythrocyte (IRBC) rheology (increased rigidity for P. falciparum IRBC, reduced rigidity but increased fragility for P. vivax IRBC).
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about parasite biology.

claim: P. vivax modifies the infected erythrocyte rheology by reducing rigidity but increasing fragility.
source: Along its intraerythrocytic development, Plasmodium spp. modifies the infected erythrocyte (IRBC) rheology (increased rigidity for P. falciparum IRBC, reduced rigidity but increased fragility for P. vivax IRBC).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior research (Handayani et al., 2009; Chotivanich et al., 2002).

claim: Alteration of IRBC rheology increases the susceptibility of IRBC to splenic clearance.
source: Such alteration increases the susceptibility of IRBC to splenic clearance (Handayani et al., 2009; Chotivanich et al., 2002); however, the parasites have developed escape strategies to avoid splenic elimination.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Malaria parasites have developed escape strategies to avoid splenic elimination.
source: Such alteration increases the susceptibility of IRBC to splenic clearance (Handayani et al., 2009; Chotivanich et al., 2002); however, the parasites have developed escape strategies to avoid splenic elimination.
evidence: This is a general statement about parasite biology supported by the context of the manuscript and established knowledge.

claim: P. falciparum expresses adhesins on the IRBC that mediate adhesion to endothelial cells, resulting in deep microvasculature sequestration.
source: For instance, P. falciparum expresses adhesins on the IRBC that mediate adhesion to the endothelial cells, resulting in deep microvasculature sequestration (Sherman et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: An IRBC can bind directly to uninfected red blood cells (URBC) to form a 'rosette'.
source: Additionally, an IRBC can bind directly to uninfected red blood cells (URBC) to form a 'rosette' (Russell and Cooke, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The rosetting phenomenon has been described in all human malaria parasites.
source: This rosetting phenomenon has been described in all human malaria parasites (Angus et al., 1996); however, the functional importance of rosetting remains ambigous (Clough et al., 1998; Wahlgren et al., 1989).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The functional importance of rosetting remains ambiguous.
source: This rosetting phenomenon has been described in all human malaria parasites (Angus et al., 1996); however, the functional importance of rosetting remains ambigous (Clough et al., 1998; Wahlgren et al., 1989).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The supposed role of rosetting in facilitation of merozoite invasion of URBC is unlikely.
source: While the supposed role of rosetting in facilitation of merozoite invasion of URBC is unlikely; recent studies show that rosette formation may have a role in parasite immune-evasion (Clough et al., 1998; Deans and Rowe, 2006; Lee et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2016; Moll et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Recent studies show that rosette formation may have a role in parasite immune-evasion.
source: While the supposed role of rosetting in facilitation of merozoite invasion of URBC is unlikely; recent studies show that rosette formation may have a role in parasite immune-evasion (Clough et al., 1998; Deans and Rowe, 2006; Lee et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2016; Moll et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The masking of rosetting IRBC with URBC may hamper IRBC recognition and therefore their clearance by the host immune system.
source: Theoretically, the masking of rosetting IRBC with URBC may hamper IRBC recognition and therefore their clearance by the host immune system (Moll et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a theoretical claim supported by a citation and logical inference.

claim: Rosetting has been associated (in some but not all studies) with disease severity.
source: Notably, rosetting has been associated (in some but not all studies) with disease severity (Treutiger et al., 1992; Carlson et al., 1994; Rowe et al., 1995; Doumbo et al., 2009; al-Yaman et al., 1995; Ho et al., 1991).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Addition of leukocytes increased the rosetting rates of various P. falciparum isolates.
source: Here, we observed that the addition of leukocytes increased the rosetting rates of various P. falciparum and P. vivax isolates.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1B.

claim: Addition of leukocytes increased the rosetting rates of various P. vivax isolates.
source: Here, we observed that the addition of leukocytes increased the rosetting rates of various P. falciparum and P. vivax isolates.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1B.

claim: IRBC stimulated monocytes to secrete products capable of stimulating rosetting.
source: We next demonstrated that IRBC stimulated monocytes to secrete products capable of stimulating rosetting, the most important being insulin growth factor binding protein 7 (IGFBP7).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data including culture supernatant experiments and ELISA quantification.

claim: The most important monocyte-secreted product capable of stimulating rosetting is insulin growth factor binding protein 7 (IGFBP7).
source: We next demonstrated that IRBC stimulated monocytes to secrete products capable of stimulating rosetting, the most important being insulin growth factor binding protein 7 (IGFBP7).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data including antibody neutralization assays and knockdown experiments.

claim: IGFBP7-mediated rosetting was different from type I rosetting.
source: We further showed that IGFBP7-mediated rosetting was different from the previously described rosetting (defined here as type I rosetting), where it (we refer to this as type II rosetting) required additional serum factors to occur, in addition to the interaction between the parasite-derived ligand on IRBC surface and the receptor on the surface of URBC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing the requirement for VWF and TSP-1 in addition to IGFBP7.

claim: Type II rosetting required additional serum factors to occur, in addition to the interaction between the parasite-derived ligand on IRBC surface and the receptor on the surface of URBC.
source: We further showed that IGFBP7-mediated rosetting was different from the previously described rosetting (defined here as type I rosetting), where it (we refer to this as type II rosetting) required additional serum factors to occur, in addition to the interaction between the parasite-derived ligand on IRBC surface and the receptor on the surface of URBC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing the requirement for VWF and TSP-1.

claim: IGFBP7-mediated type II rosetting reduced phagocytosis by monocytes.
source: Functionally, we observed that the IGFBP7-mediated type II rosetting reduced phagocytosis by monocytes, and therefore defined a new escape mechanism for the malaria parasites.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing reduced phagocytosis rates when IRBC were pre-incubated with IGFBP7.

claim: IGFBP7-mediated type II rosetting defines a new escape mechanism for the malaria parasites.
source: Functionally, we observed that the IGFBP7-mediated type II rosetting reduced phagocytosis by monocytes, and therefore defined a new escape mechanism for the malaria parasites.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing reduced phagocytosis.

claim: P. falciparum- and P. vivax-IRBC formed rosettes in the presence of 20% autologous human serum.
source: P. falciparum- and P. vivax-IRBC formed rosettes (Figure 1A, top panel) in the presence of 20% autologous human serum and the extent of rosetting at baseline is variable depending on the parasite isolates (Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and cited prior research.

claim: The extent of rosetting at baseline is variable depending on the parasite isolates.
source: P. falciparum- and P. vivax-IRBC formed rosettes (Figure 1A, top panel) in the presence of 20% autologous human serum and the extent of rosetting at baseline is variable depending on the parasite isolates (Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: When autologous blood leukocytes were incubated with clinical isolates, the rosetting rate increased by 10–40% depending on individual isolates for both parasite species.
source: When autologous blood leukocytes were incubated with clinical isolates, the rosetting rate increased by 10–40% depending on individual isolates for both parasite species (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The rosette-stimulation effect of leukocytes was mediated primarily by monocytes.
source: This effect was mediated primarily by monocytes (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C comparing monocytes and neutrophils.

claim: The rosette-stimulation mediated by THP-1 was similar to that of peripheral monocytes.
source: The rosette-stimulation mediated by THP-1 was similar to that of peripheral monocytes (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Addition of undifferentiated THP-1 (UT) increased rosetting rates in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Addition of undifferentiated THP-1 (UT) and macrophage-like THP-1 (MT) increased rosetting rates in a dose-dependent manner.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Addition of macrophage-like THP-1 (MT) increased rosetting rates in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Addition of undifferentiated THP-1 (UT) and macrophage-like THP-1 (MT) increased rosetting rates in a dose-dependent manner.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: MT were more potent than UT in stimulating rosetting, where the difference increased with the number of cells added.
source: MT were more potent than UT, where the difference increased with the number of cells added (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Culture supernatants (CS) of both THP-1 cell types showed similar rosette-stimulation effects.
source: Culture supernatants (CS) of both THP-1 cell types showed similar rosette-stimulation effects (Figure 1F), with CSMT exerting a higher degree of rosette-stimulation than CSUT.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: CSMT exerted a higher degree of rosette-stimulation than CSUT.
source: Culture supernatants (CS) of both THP-1 cell types showed similar rosette-stimulation effects (Figure 1F), with CSMT exerting a higher degree of rosette-stimulation than CSUT.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The rosette-stimulating factors were in the aqueous fraction of CSMT.
source: Fractionation of CSMT into aqueous and lipid fractions revealed that the rosette-stimulating factors were in the aqueous fraction (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Both aqueous sub-fractions (high and low molecular weight) induced rosetting of P. falciparum.
source: Subsequently, we further fractionated the aqueous fraction into high and low molecular weight sub-fractions (with a cut-off of 30 kDa). Both aqueous sub-fractions induced rosetting of P. falciparum and P. vivax (Figure 2B and C), demonstrating that the rosetting stimulation was mediated by multiple secreted hydrophilic factors, predominantly of sizes ≤ 30 kDa (particularly for P. falciparum).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Both aqueous sub-fractions (high and low molecular weight) induced rosetting of P. vivax.
source: Subsequently, we further fractionated the aqueous fraction into high and low molecular weight sub-fractions (with a cut-off of 30 kDa). Both aqueous sub-fractions induced rosetting of P. falciparum and P. vivax (Figure 2B and C), demonstrating that the rosetting stimulation was mediated by multiple secreted hydrophilic factors, predominantly of sizes ≤ 30 kDa (particularly for P. falciparum).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The rosetting stimulation was mediated by multiple secreted hydrophilic factors, predominantly of sizes ≤ 30 kDa (particularly for P. falciparum).
source: Subsequently, we further fractionated the aqueous fraction into high and low molecular weight sub-fractions (with a cut-off of 30 kDa). Both aqueous sub-fractions induced rosetting of P. falciparum and P. vivax (Figure 2B and C), demonstrating that the rosetting stimulation was mediated by multiple secreted hydrophilic factors, predominantly of sizes ≤ 30 kDa (particularly for P. falciparum).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that both fractions induced rosetting, with the ≤30 kDa fraction being more potent.

claim: Heating of CSMT's ≤ 30 kDa aqueous fraction at 56°C for 1 h did not completely abolish its rosette-stimulating effect.
source: Heating of CSMT's ≤ 30 kDa aqueous fraction at 56°C for 1 h did not completely abolish its rosette-stimulating effect (Figure 2D), indicating the presence of heat-stable factors.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The presence of heat-stable factors is indicated by the partial retention of rosette-stimulating effect after heating.
source: Heating of CSMT's ≤ 30 kDa aqueous fraction at 56°C for 1 h did not completely abolish its rosette-stimulating effect (Figure 2D), indicating the presence of heat-stable factors.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing partial retention of activity after heating.

claim: Mass spectrometry analysis identified 694 proteins in the ≤ 30 kDa aqueous fraction.
source: To further investigate the potential stimulating factors, mass spectrometry analysis was performed on this fraction. We identified 694 proteins (Supplementary file 2), of which complement factor D (CFD), insulin-like growth factor binding protein 7 (IGFBP7), nidogen 1 (NID1), hyaluronan-binding protein 2 (HABP2), and periostin (OSF2) were shortlisted (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: Complement factor D (CFD), insulin-like growth factor binding protein 7 (IGFBP7), nidogen 1 (NID1), hyaluronan-binding protein 2 (HABP2), and periostin (OSF2) were shortlisted from the mass spectrometry analysis.
source: To further investigate the potential stimulating factors, mass spectrometry analysis was performed on this fraction. We identified 694 proteins (Supplementary file 2), of which complement factor D (CFD), insulin-like growth factor binding protein 7 (IGFBP7), nidogen 1 (NID1), hyaluronan-binding protein 2 (HABP2), and periostin (OSF2) were shortlisted (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by mass spectrometry data and selection criteria based on protein properties.

claim: The shortlisted molecules were selected because they are secreted proteins and possess cell adhesion-related properties associated with pathological changes such as vascular injuries, inflammation, cancer development, and leukocyte recruitment.
source: Apart from having high scores in the mass spectrometry analysis (Supplementary file 2), these molecules were selected because they are secreted proteins and possess cell adhesion-related properties associated with pathological changes such as vascular injuries, inflammation, cancer development, and leukocyte recruitment (UniProt Consortium, 2015; St Croix et al., 2000; Mambetsariev et al., 2010; Ulazzi et al., 2007; Schwanekamp et al., 2016; Lindner et al., 2005; Markiewski and Lambris, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research and database information.

claim: Antibody neutralization of IGFBP7 significantly reduced (by ~40%) the rosette-stimulation by CSMT for both parasite species.
source: Antibody neutralization of IGFBP7 significantly reduced (by ~40%) the rosette-stimulation by CSMT for both parasite species (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Rosette-stimulation by CSMT was reduced by anti-CFD antibodies, albeit to a lesser extent than anti-IGFBP7.
source: Rosette-stimulation by CSMT was also reduced by anti-CFD (Figure 3B) and anti-OSF2 (Figure 3C) antibodies, albeit to a lesser extent.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Rosette-stimulation by CSMT was reduced by anti-OSF2 antibodies, albeit to a lesser extent than anti-IGFBP7.
source: Rosette-stimulation by CSMT was also reduced by anti-CFD (Figure 3B) and anti-OSF2 (Figure 3C) antibodies, albeit to a lesser extent.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Antibodies against NID1 had no effect on CSMT-mediated rosette-stimulation.
source: Antibodies against NID1 (Figure 3D) and HABP2 (Figure 3E) had no effect on CSMT-mediated rosette-stimulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Antibodies against HABP2 had no effect on CSMT-mediated rosette-stimulation.
source: Antibodies against NID1 (Figure 3D) and HABP2 (Figure 3E) had no effect on CSMT-mediated rosette-stimulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Addition of human recombinant IGFBP7 to leukocyte-free parasite culture stimulated rosette formation in a dose-dependent and satiable manner for P. falciparum isolates.
source: Addition of human recombinant IGFBP7 to leukocyte-free parasite culture stimulated rosette formation in a dose-dependent and satiable manner for P. falciparum and P. vivax isolates, reaching a plateau at 100 ng/ml (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Addition of human recombinant IGFBP7 to leukocyte-free parasite culture stimulated rosette formation in a dose-dependent and satiable manner for P. vivax isolates.
source: Addition of human recombinant IGFBP7 to leukocyte-free parasite culture stimulated rosette formation in a dose-dependent and satiable manner for P. falciparum and P. vivax isolates, reaching a plateau at 100 ng/ml (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: IGFBP7-mediated rosette formation reached a plateau at 100 ng/ml.
source: Addition of human recombinant IGFBP7 to leukocyte-free parasite culture stimulated rosette formation in a dose-dependent and satiable manner for P. falciparum and P. vivax isolates, reaching a plateau at 100 ng/ml (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4A and 4B.

claim: For P. falciparum, no significant difference in rosette-stimulatory effect between the CSMT and IGFBP7 was found.
source: For P. falciparum, no significant difference in rosette-stimulatory effect between the CSMT and IGFBP7 was found (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: P. vivax rosette-stimulation by CSMT was significantly higher than that by recombinant IGFBP7 alone.
source: On the contrary, P. vivax rosette-stimulation by CSMT was significantly higher than that by recombinant IGFBP7 alone (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The rosette-stimulating capacity of IGFBP7 was abolished by heat denaturation at 95°C for 1 h.
source: The rosette-stimulating capacity of IGFBP7 was abolished by heat denaturation at 95°C for 1 h (Figure 4E and F), thus eliminating the possibility that the effect was caused by a non-protein contaminant in the recombinant protein preparation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 4E and 4F.

claim: Heat denaturation of IGFBP7 eliminates the possibility that the rosette-stimulating effect was caused by a non-protein contaminant in the recombinant protein preparation.
source: The rosette-stimulating capacity of IGFBP7 was abolished by heat denaturation at 95°C for 1 h (Figure 4E and F), thus eliminating the possibility that the effect was caused by a non-protein contaminant in the recombinant protein preparation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing loss of activity after heat denaturation.

claim: The IGFBP7 binding-inducing effect was only observed when URBC and IRBC were present in the culture.
source: Furthermore, the IGFBP7 binding-inducing effect was only observed when URBC and IRBC were present in the culture.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Incubation of URBC alone with IGFBP7 did not induce clustering effect on the cells.
source: Incubation of URBC alone with IGFBP7 did not induce clustering effect on the cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1; top panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: IGFBP7 required a minimum of 15 min to significantly stimulate rosetting.
source: IGFBP7 required a minimum of 15 min to significantly stimulate rosetting.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The rosette-stimulating effect of IGFBP7 did not significantly increase further after 15 minutes.
source: However, the rosette-stimulating effect did not significantly increase further afterwards (Figure 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: IGFBP7-mediated rosetting was a reversible event, where removal of the protein from the system reverted the rosetting rates to their baseline values as fast as 15 min post-protein removal.
source: Importantly, IGFBP7-mediated rosetting was a reversible event, where removal of the protein from the system reverted the rosetting rates to their baseline values (rosetting rates recorded prior to IGFBP7 exposure) as fast as 15 min post-protein removal (Figure 4H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Trypsinization of IRBC abrogated the rosette-stimulating effect of IGFBP7.
source: Trypsinization of IRBC abrogated the rosette-stimulating effect of IGFBP7 (Figure 5A), suggesting the involvement of parasite-derived proteins expressed on the surface of IRBC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Trypsinization of IRBC suggests the involvement of parasite-derived proteins expressed on the surface of IRBC in IGFBP7-mediated rosetting.
source: Trypsinization of IRBC abrogated the rosette-stimulating effect of IGFBP7 (Figure 5A), suggesting the involvement of parasite-derived proteins expressed on the surface of IRBC.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing loss of IGFBP7 effect after trypsin treatment.

claim: P. falciparum expressed different surface antigens including rosetting ligands such as the P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane proteins 1 (PfEMP1), STEVOR, and RIFIN.
source: P. falciparum expressed different surface antigens including rosetting ligands such as the P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane proteins 1 (PfEMP1), STEVOR, and RIFIN (Chan et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The sensitivity to low level of trypsin treatment (10 µg/ml) suggested that PfEMP1, rather than STEVOR or RIFIN, was likely the adhesin involved in IGFBP7-mediated rosetting.
source: The sensitivity to low level of trypsin treatment (10 µg/ml) used here suggested that PfEMP1, rather than STEVOR or RIFIN, was likely the adhesin involved (Kyes et al., 1999; Niang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on experimental data and citations to prior research about differential trypsin sensitivity of these proteins.

claim: SBP1 transports PfEMP1 from the parasitophorous vacuole to the Maurer's cleft for subsequent assembly and export to the surface of IRBC.
source: SBP1 transports PfEMP1 from the parasitophorous vacuole to the Maurer's cleft for subsequent assembly and export to the surface of IRBC.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of SBP1.

claim: The SBP1-KO-CS2 line is unable to express PfEMP1 on the surface of the IRBC.
source: Therefore, the SBP1-KO-CS2 line is unable to express PfEMP1 on the surface of the IRBC.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known function of SBP1 and the knockout of this gene.

claim: Knock out of SBP1 gene does not affect the surface expression of STEVOR and RIFIN.
source: However, knock out of this gene does not affect the surface expression of STEVOR and RIFIN (Maier et al., 2007; Chan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: IGFBP7 increased the rosetting rate of CS2 wild-type parasite.
source: IGFBP7 increased the rosetting rate of CS2 wild-type parasite but had no effect on SBP1-KO-CS2 rosetting (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: IGFBP7 had no effect on SBP1-KO-CS2 rosetting.
source: IGFBP7 increased the rosetting rate of CS2 wild-type parasite but had no effect on SBP1-KO-CS2 rosetting (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The rosetting machinery of NF54_VAR2CSA_WT responded positively to the presence of IGFBP7.
source: The rosetting machinery of NF54_VAR2CSA_WT responded positively to the presence of IGFBP7.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The rosetting rates of NF54_T934D clone (lacking PfEMP1 on the surface of IRBC) were not significantly altered by IGFBP7.
source: On the other hand, the rosetting rates of NF54_T934D clone (lacking PfEMP1 on the surface of IRBC) were not significantly altered by IGFBP7 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: IRBCs with surface expression of PfEMP1 variant VAR2CSA did not form many rosettes.
source: Of note, IRBCs with surface expression of PfEMP1 variant VAR2CSA (which include the CS2_WT and NF54_VAR2CSA_WT) did not form many rosettes, which was in parallel with earlier report (Rogerson et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observation and a citation to prior research.

claim: The rosettes formed by NF54_VAR2CSA_WT were small.
source: In addition, the rosettes formed by NF54_VAR2CSA_WT (Figure 5C, inset i) and NF54_T934D (Figure 5C, inset ii) were small.
evidence: This claim is supported by visual observation in Figure 5C inset i.

claim: The rosettes formed by NF54_T934D were small.
source: In addition, the rosettes formed by NF54_VAR2CSA_WT (Figure 5C, inset i) and NF54_T934D (Figure 5C, inset ii) were small.
evidence: This claim is supported by visual observation in Figure 5C inset ii.

claim: PfEMP1 is the first rosetting ligand to be expressed on the surface of IRBC (as early as late ring stage).
source: For example, PfEMP1 is the first rosetting ligand to be expressed on the surface of IRBC (as early as late ring stage), followed by RIFIN, and finally STEVOR (which are at the much more mature stages) (Kyes et al., 2000; Lavazec et al., 2007; Kaviratne et al., 2002; Bachmann et al., 2012; Niang et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: PfEMP1 is the only rosetting ligand available on the surface of late ring-IRBCs.
source: In other words, PfEMP1 is the only rosetting ligand available on the surface of late ring-IRBCs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the sequential expression pattern of rosetting ligands cited from prior research.

claim: IGFBP7 significantly increased the rates of rosette formation by the late ring stages of P. falciparum.
source: We performed the IGFBP7-rosetting assessment on the late ring stages (~hour 16–26) of a laboratory-adapted clinical isolate (nine replicates across three different cycles) and found that IGFBP7 significantly increased the rates of rosette formation (Figure 5D) by the late ring stages (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: PfEMP1 is essential for IGFBP7-mediated rosetting in P. falciparum.
source: Taken together, these results suggest strongly that PfEMP1 is essential for IGFBP7-mediated rosetting in P. falciparum.
